subject: Mutual Action Plan: performance evaluation scope, SLOs & close timeline
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aceta.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual action plan & perf scope for pilot

Hi Rachel / team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost points looked promising. As discussed, the next step for us is a short pilot MAP that proves the performance story for our user-facing assistant. Specifically we need a benchmarking plan in the MAP that covers:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) for cold and warm starts
- Sustained throughput and token/sec for concurrent sessions
- Percentile latency (p50/p90/p95) at realistic request sizes
- Concurrency targets (we expect up to 120 concurrent active users at peak)

Can you share a proposed MAP section that scopes the workload, defines success criteria/SLOs, and a close timeline (we want to decide by end of October if we move to Dedicated)? Procurement will also need a short acceptance checklist for signoff.

Example constraints from our side: 1) 16k token average context for retrieval-augmented prompts, 2) many short interactions (1-3 generated tokens most of the time), 3) occasional long generations (up to 512 tokens).

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, Aceta Health
samir.patel@aceta.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aceta.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf scope for pilot

Samir — thanks, great summary. Attached is a short MAP draft (map_draft_v1.pdf) with the benchmarking playbook we propose. Key points (high level):

Workload slices (proposed):
- Slice A — Conversation starters: 90% requests, short responses (1–3 tokens), median prompt length ~600 tokens. Goal: low TTFT, preserve p95 < 250ms on warm cache.
- Slice B — Retrieval-heavy: 8% requests, long context (~16k tokens), short generations. Goal: p95 TTFT < 400ms, warm cache.
- Slice C — Long generation: 2% requests, up to 512 tokens output. Goal: steady-state token/sec throughput targets and p95 token latency budget.

Concurrency plan: run tests at 1 / 10 / 50 / 120 concurrent sessions (ramp up over a single day). For each concurrency tier we measure: p50/p90/p95 total TTFT, tokens/sec, tail latency for first token, and error rates.

Success criteria / acceptance gates (draft):
- Functional: no more than 0.5% request errors during benchmark window.
- Latency: p95 TTFT must be below agreed SLOs per slice (see table in attachment).
- Throughput: System must sustain target tokens/sec for the long-generation slice for at least 10 minutes without degradation.
- Stability: No sustained memory growth across runs; KV cache hit-rate above 70% for Slice A.

Suggested SLOs (proposal):
- Slice A (warm path): p95 TTFT < 250ms, p50 < 80ms
- Slice B (large context): p95 TTFT < 400ms
- Slice C (long gen): sustained >= 20 tokens/sec per worker at p95 token latency budget of 120ms

Run plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (next 3 business days): finalize MAP workload profiles + signoff
- Week 1: dry run internal — sanity and instrumentation checks
- Week 2: formal benchmarking runs (3 test windows)
- Week 3: results review, remediation plan if needed, and acceptance signoff

Related attachments: map_draft_v1.pdf (bench playbook, test cases, sample report template).

If this looks good we can lock a run window next Tuesday-Wednesday (Oct 20–21). Jonas / Marcus — can you add the loadgen config and a concise set of workload profiles to the MAP?

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aceta.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf scope for pilot

Forwarding the initial workload artifacts we used for the demo so they can be incorporated into the MAP. Attachments: workload_profiles.csv, loadgen_config.yaml.

Notes / clarifications (quick):
- workload_profiles.csv contains three rows (slice A/B/C) with field-level distributions for prompt tokens, generation length, KV cache usage, and request inter-arrival times.
- loadgen_config.yaml contains the redwood-loadgen settings we recommend: continuous mode for concurrency stress, 10s warmup, 5m steady window, 2m cooldown. Use client-side tracing enabled and push traces to the MAP run folder.

Recommended run parameters for acceptance run:
- Ramp: 0 -> target concurrency over 90s
- Warmup: 2 minutes (to populate cache for Slice A)
- Steady: 10 minutes per tier (collect p50/p90/p95 and token/sec)
- Repeat: 3 runs per tier across different times of day to capture variance

I set conservative SLOs in the CSV (p95 numbers are slightly above Rachel's proposal) — agree we should finalize by end of today so Samir can get procurement aligned.

--Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aceta.com>

Appreciate the speed here — the draft looks good. A couple of asks before we lock a run window:
- Can we get an explicit acceptance checklist for procurement (short measurable bullets)?
- Our target commercial decision date is Oct 29. We need a final performance report + a short remediation plan by Oct 26 to make that call.
- DocuSign to be routed to legal@aceta.com after acceptance.

If you can confirm the final SLO numbers and the run dates (Oct 20/21 or Oct 22/23 window) we'll confirm internally and route procurement.

Thanks,
Samir

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aceta.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-17T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf scope for pilot

Samir — agreed on timeline and doc routing. Final notes and deliverables (this email will be added to the MAP doc):

Final SLOs (locked for run):
- Slice A (warm): p95 TTFT < 260ms, p50 < 85ms
- Slice B (large context): p95 TTFT < 420ms
- Slice C (long gen): sustained >= 18 tokens/sec, p95 token latency < 150ms

Procurement acceptance checklist (to include in MAP):
- Bench report with raw traces and summary (CSV + PDF)
- Signed acceptance statement from Aceta Ops (email or DocuSign)
- Error rate verification: observed error rate <= 0.5% across runs
- Stability verification: no OOMs, and memory utilization within expected bounds across 3 repeated runs
- Performance regression check vs. baseline (demo run) — no >10% regression on p95 for Slice A

Proposed run window: Oct 21 (Tiered runs at 09:00, 13:00, 17:00 PT) — we will run the three concurrency tiers across the day and deliver preliminary numbers by Oct 22 morning. Full report and remediation plan by Oct 26.

DocuSign link (once you confirm): https://docusign.com/link/ABC12345
MAP artifact locations: https://redwood.app/hubspot/record/ACETA-PL-2026-09

Next steps: Samir to confirm run window and routing address for DocuSign (legal@aceta.com). Jonas / Marcus to ensure loadgen is ready and attach the final workload_profiles.csv to the MAP. I'll schedule the report review meeting for Oct 26.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—Rachel
